title: Servicing Manual, Deficiency Balance Accounts: One Account per Liquidated Contract
content:
**Clause.** A Deficiency Balance Account is held per liquidated contract: a borrower may hold several deficiency accounts, one for each contract whose vehicle was sold with a deficiency, without a per-borrower limit, and a contract never has more than one deficiency account (the deficiency accounts per liquidated contract figure of the band schedule).

## The clause in parts

| Question the clause answers | Answer |
|---|---|
| What is a Deficiency Balance Account attached to? | One liquidated contract whose vehicle was sold with a deficiency |
| How many deficiency accounts may one borrower hold? | One per such contract; there is no per-borrower limit |
| How many deficiency accounts may one contract have? | Never more than one |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A borrower had two contracts, and the vehicles of both were sold with a deficiency. The borrower holds two Deficiency Balance Accounts, one for each contract.
- A borrower had two contracts, and only one vehicle was sold with a deficiency. The borrower holds one Deficiency Balance Account, for that contract.
- A single liquidated contract never carries a second deficiency account.
